ACCEPTThe aligned EAST/EAST batch inequality and the explicit unbounded  $2-n$  marginal are correct under the stated hypotheses. The debit is assigned to each contacted root, with at most one debit per root; no argument limits a receiving  $V$  to one contacted root. The common-baseline adjustments  $a_i$  remain in the exact ledger throughout.There is one false arithmetic sentence in the construction proof that should be corrected:
$$s_i=t_i-6=t_{i-1}+4$$
is the preceding root’s far-tip row, not four rows after that tip. The construction remains endpoint-disjoint because the relevant columns are separated. I give the precise replacement and an all- $n$  proof below.I have not independently rerun the new checker or Lean audits. This verdict rests on the supplied immutable constructors and the general arguments below.1. Owner injection counts each new source exactly onceThe source charges distinguish the two roles:
$$\operatorname{charge}(O_i)=+1,\qquad
\operatorname{charge}(V_i)=-1.$$
Thus no original record can be both an  $O$  and a  $V$ .For  $O_i$ , its near column is the minimum endpoint column. The last endpoint in that column is
$$p_i+(5,0).$$
Consequently the immutable endpoint set determines  $p_i$ . Distinct root sites therefore give distinct  $O_i$ .For  $V_i$ , the supplied full-U constructor has exactly two degree-one endpoints, its leg tips. Under the stipulated even translations:The near tip  $x_i=p_i+(-3,-1)$  has even row and even column.The far tip has even row and odd column.Hence the unique even/even terminal determines  $x_i$ , and therefore  $p_i$ . Distinct root sites give distinct  $V_i$ .Together with the assumption that all these originals are outside  $B$ , this proves that all  $2n$  new source contributions are counted once. Each contributes one to  $N+S$ , despite the two different charge signs.This argument uses the fixed EAST/EAST orientation and even translations. It makes no appeal to a complete extension.2. The aligned negative-U packing argument is validHere the packing lemma is applied to the downward U records in the displayed EAST phase. That orientation is part of the setting and is also built into the Lean endpoint definition.Let two such originals have even bar tops  $s_1\le s_2$ . Suppose endpoints  $z_1,z_2$  share a physical tile.Because the second endpoint has row at least the even integer  $s_2$ , the first endpoint also has row at least  $s_2$ . Moreover, the second bar’s column interval starts even and ends odd. It therefore contains the entire physical tile column containing  $z_2$ , including the column of  $z_1$ .Now:If  $s_1=s_2$ , the first bar contains the point  $(s_2,z_{1,c})$ .If  $s_1<s_2$ , parity gives  $s_2\ge s_1+2$ . The first endpoint lies below its bar, on a continuous leg, which also contains  $(s_2,z_{1,c})$ .The second bar contains that same point. This contradicts endpoint disjointness.Thus
$$\operatorname{Foot}(V_i)\cap\operatorname{Foot}(V_j)=\varnothing
\qquad(i\ne j).$$
The argument works for negative coordinates and unbounded widths and depths. It uses actual interval containment, not a finite catalogue.The opposite-phase example is also correct.  $U(8,10,10)$  at offset  $(0,0)$  and its translate by  $(4,8)$  are endpoint-disjoint positive originals and share precisely the four tiles with top-left coordinates
$$(4,8),\quad(6,8),\quad(8,8),\quad(10,8).$$
For clarity, I would make the lemma’s opening explicitly say “a downward full U in the displayed EAST phase.” Its proof uses downward stems as well as the stated column alignment; the batch setting already supplies that restriction.3. Root near protection leaves only the far boundary availableFor each root, in its own translated local chart, all physical tiles in columns  $C-1,C$  that contain an  $O$  endpoint are full in  $H_i+O_i+V_i$ :Tile top rowLeft-column occupantsRight-column occupants $t,t+2,\ldots,20$  $V_i,V_i$  $O_i,O_i$  $22$  $V_i,P_0$  $O_i,O_i$  $24,26,28$  $P_0,P_0$  $O_i,O_i$  $30$  $P_0,P_0$  $O_i,Q$ The first range can be empty. Every bar-interior tile is full within  $O_i$  itself.Because all foreign new originals are distinct from these owners and endpoint-disjoint from them, no foreign endpoint can occupy any cell of one of these full tiles. Therefore a foreign new original can meet  $O_i$ ’s footprint only in its far boundary tile column.For comparisons between different instances, use common physical coordinates, absorbing the even translations. Let  $X_i$  be the root’s even far column and  $[T_i,U_i]$  its even-start, even-tip far interval. Its available far tiles have columns
$$X_i,\ X_i+1.$$
Two roots cannot share one of these tiles. Such a shared tile would force equality of their even far columns. Their tile-row overlap would then contain a common actual even endpoint row, giving an endpoint collision.Together with V/V packing, this proves that every new/new shared tile involves exactly one root and one  $V$ . In particular, no tile can support two different foreign contacts.4. The foreign-port argument is correctly one-per-rootConsider a foreign contact  $O_i/V_j$ , with  $j\ne i$ .A  $V_j$  bar fills each physical tile it meets, so a root endpoint cannot share one of its bar tiles.Nor can the contact use  $V_j$ ’s near stem: its column and  $O_i$ ’s far column are both even. Sharing a tile would force equality of those columns and a common actual even endpoint row.The contact must therefore use the odd far stem of  $V_j$ , in column
$$X_i+1.$$
Write its physical far interval as  $[S_j,W_j]$ , with even endpoints. A shared tile implies an actual common even row, so
$$S_j\le U_i,\qquad W_j\ge T_i.$$
If  $S_j\ge T_i$ , the  $V_j$  bar lies at a row in  $O_i$ ’s far interval. That bar contains the point
$$(S_j,X_i),$$
because  $X_i$  is immediately left of its far endpoint column. This would collide with  $O_i$ .Hence
$$S_j<T_i,\qquad W_j\ge T_i,$$
and every  $V_j$  contacting  $O_i$  contains the same endpoint
$$\boxed{(T_i,X_i+1)}.$$
Endpoint disjointness therefore permits at most one such  $V_j$  for each root  $O_i$ .When  $\eta_i=1$ , the root’s own  $V_i$  already occupies this point. No foreign  $V_j$  can then contact it. Thus, for the foreign-contact set
$$\mathcal C=\{(i,j):i\ne j,\ \operatorname{Foot}(O_i)\cap
\operatorname{Foot}(V_j)\ne\varnothing\},$$
we have
$$|\mathcal C|\le \#\{i:\eta_i=0\}=r.$$
There is no corresponding bound on the number of different  $i$  associated with one  $j$ . A single  $V_j$  may contact many roots, along disjoint bands of its far stem.5. The signed correction of each contact is exactNo vertical cross event is possibleEvery odd-row endpoint of every new U has its preceding even-row endpoint in the same column and in the same original. This holds both on the inner bar row and along the continuous legs.A vertical intratile edge joins an even-row cell to the following odd-row cell. If those cells belonged to different new owners, the odd-row owner would also contain the even-row cell, contradicting endpoint disjointness.Thus all new/new cross events are horizontal.One foreign contact contributes  $-1+2\varepsilon$ For  $O_i/V_j$ , put
$$w=\min(U_i,W_j),\qquad q=\frac{w-T_i}{2}.$$
The overlap begins at  $T_i$ , because  $S_j<T_i$ , and ends at the even row  $w$ .The immutable support phases give exactly: $O_i\to V_j$  at odd rows  $T_i+1,\ldots,w-1$ ; $V_j\to O_i$  at even rows  $T_i,\ldots,w$ .There are therefore
$$2q+1$$
cross events.The  $q$  tiles with top rows
$$T_i,T_i+2,\ldots,w-2$$
are full using the two new owners. They are cooperative: neither individual pair addition could supply the other pair’s cells.At the terminal overlap tile, both upper cells are occupied by these new owners, but at least one lower cell is missing from them. No third new owner can fill it, since that would create either O/O or V/V tile overlap. Any completion must therefore come from  $B$ .Let  $\varepsilon_{ij}=1$  if this terminal tile is completed by old endpoints, and  $0$  otherwise. The contact’s exact contribution is
$$\boxed{
2(q+\varepsilon_{ij})-(2q+1)
=-1+2\varepsilon_{ij}.}$$
This includes  $q=0$ : one cross event, no earlier full tile, and possibly an old-completed terminal tile.All new/old events in the terminal tile already belong to the corresponding individual gains  $g_i,g_j$ . They are not counted again in this cross correction.Since different contacts have disjoint tiles and event sets, one obtains the stronger exact description
$$C_{\mathrm{new/new}}
=-|\mathcal C|+2\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal C}\varepsilon_{ij}.$$
Consequently
$$\boxed{C_{\mathrm{new/new}}\ge-|\mathcal C|\ge-r.}$$
6. The common-baseline partition and credit allocation are soundFix one global labelling of the originals in  $B$  and all the pairs.Let
$$F_i=F(B+P_i)\setminus F(B).$$
A tile in  $F_i$  contains a cell absent from  $B$  that is supplied by  $P_i$ . An endpoint-disjoint  $P_j$  cannot supply that same cell. Hence the  $F_i$  are pairwise disjoint.Moreover, a tile in  $F_i$  is already fully occupied by  $B+P_i$ , so it cannot contain an endpoint of another new pair.Conversely, a newly full tile not in any  $F_i$  must contain endpoints from at least two new pairs. Otherwise it would already be full after the corresponding individual addition. This gives the exact full-tile partition
$$F\!\left(B+\bigcup_iP_i\right)\setminus F(B)
=
\bigsqcup_i F_i\;\sqcup\;F_{\mathrm{cooperative}}.$$
For events, the exact partition is into:Old events, which remain unchanged.New events involving  $B$  and one pair, or internal to one pair.Events between different new pairs.The second class is the disjoint union of the individual addition event sets. The third is  $E_{\mathrm{cross}}$ . Fixed source labels and immutable support exclusions are essential here and are used correctly.Because the new source contributions also add once,
$$\Phi\!\left(B+\bigcup_iP_i\right)-\Phi(B)
=\sum_i g_i+C_{\mathrm{new/new}}
=\sum_i(\ell_i+a_i)+C_{\mathrm{new/new}}.$$
Finally,
$$\kappa_i=1\Longrightarrow\eta_i=1.$$
Therefore:If  $\eta_i=0$ , then  $\kappa_i=0$  and
$$\ell_i=2-\delta_{0,i}\ge1.$$
If  $\eta_i=1$ , the root-pair formula gives  $\ell_i\ge0$ .Thus
$$\ell_i-\mathbf 1_{\{\eta_i=0\}}\ge0,$$
which proves both inequalities in (2).The nonreuse point is precise: a receiving  $V_j$ ’s source contribution remains in its own pair gain exactly once. Its contacts with other roots are paid from the gains of those distinct contacted root pairs. Each such root is charged at most once.Nothing in this argument supplies a sign for  $a_i$ . Enlarging  $H_i$  to  $B$  can add old/new events as well as full-tile completions; that is exactly the adjustment retained in the formula.7. The explicit construction works for every  $n$ Set
$$q_i=n-1-i.$$
Then the displayed parameters simplify to
$$t_i=-10q_i,\qquad
B_{0,i}=8+100q_i,\qquad
s_i=t_i-6.$$
All roots therefore have even breadth at least eight and admissible even incident depth  $30-t_i$ .For  $V_0$ ,
$$B=B_{0,0}+2,\qquad
d=28-t_0,\qquad
f=8-t_0.$$
Its far column is  $X+1$ , and its far tip is
$$s_0+f=(t_0-6)+(8-t_0)=2.$$
For  $i\ge1$ ,
$$B=6,\qquad d=28-t_i,\qquad f=4,$$
so its far column and tip are
$$C_i+4,\qquad t_i-2.$$
This exactly satisfies the local narrow-breadth frontier.Consequently
$$\eta_0=1,\qquad \eta_i=0\ (i\ge1),\qquad
\delta_{0,i}=\kappa_i=0,$$
and
$$\ell_0=1,\qquad \ell_i=2\ (i\ge1).$$
Correct the erroneous row comparisonThe note’s sentence about beginning four rows after the preceding far tip is false:
$$t_{i-1}=t_i-10,\qquad
t_{i-1}+4=t_i-6=s_i.$$
For example, at  $n=2$ , the preceding root’s far tip and  $V_1$ ’s bar top are both at row  $-6$ .A correct replacement is:For  $i\ge1$ ,  $V_i$ ’s far stem ends at  $t_i-2$ , and its bar starts at  $s_i=t_{i-1}+4$ , the preceding root’s far-tip row. Its rightmost endpoint column is  $C_i+4\le X-3$ , so it stays strictly left of that tip and every root far stem.This repairs the explanation without changing any construction parameter.All old/new interactions are localFor the fixed old parameters, each  $H_i$  has endpoint columns in
$$[-34,31]+100i$$
and endpoint rows at least  $17$ .Those column intervals begin even and end odd, so they also contain their complete physical endpoint-tile footprints. The old blocks have disjoint footprints.All new bars lie above every old endpoint tile. The only new stems reaching old-block heights are the near stems, at  $C_i$  and  $C_i-1$ , whose tile column lies inside their own old block’s interval.The root far columns  $X$  and the long  $V_0$  far column  $X+1$  lie beyond the final old block’s aligned right boundary. For  $i\ge1$ , the short  $V_i$  far stem ends at  $t_i-2\le-2$ , above all old endpoint tiles.Thus the footprint of  $P_i$  meets old endpoints only in  $H_i$ . Its new full tiles and events are unchanged when the baseline is enlarged from  $H_i$  to  $\bigcup_jH_j$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{a_i=0\quad\text{for all }i.}$$
All new originals are endpoint-disjointFor  $i<j$ , root  $O_i$ ’s far stem ends at
$$t_i+4<t_j,$$
before  $O_j$  starts. Its near stem is strictly left of all  $O_j$  endpoints. Its bar is above the first row of  $O_j$ . Hence roots are pairwise disjoint.For  $i,j\ge1$ , the  $V_i$  occupy separated column intervals
$$[C_i-1,C_i+4].$$
The bar of  $V_0$  precedes every other V bar; its two stems lie respectively left and right of all those intervals. Hence the V originals are pairwise disjoint.For  $V_i$ ,  $i\ge1$ , and a foreign root  $O_j$ :If  $j>i$ , all  $V_i$  columns lie strictly left of  $O_j$ .If  $j<i$ ,  $V_i$  starts after  $O_j$ ’s bar tile, while its columns lie strictly between  $O_j$ ’s near stem and the common far stem  $X$ .These foreign pairs do not share endpoint tiles.Finally,  $V_0$ ’s bar lies above every root bar. Its near stem lies left of every foreign root, and its far stem is in column  $X+1$ , adjacent to the root far stems at  $X$ . It is endpoint-disjoint from all roots.Therefore the only foreign shared-tile contacts are exactly
$$\boxed{O_i/V_0,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n-1.}$$
Every foreign contact contributes exactly  $-1$ The overlap with  $O_i$  is
$$[t_i,\min(t_i+4,2)].$$
For a nonfinal foreign root, half its length is  $2$ ; for the final root it is  $1$ .The terminal tile is incomplete in either case. No old endpoint can fill it because its columns  $X,X+1$  lie beyond the old footprints. Thus  $\varepsilon_{i0}=0$ , and each contact contributes exactly  $-1$ .For  $n=1$ , there are no foreign contacts; all formulas remain valid.It follows that
$$\sum_i\ell_i=2n-1,\qquad
C_{\mathrm{new/new}}=-(n-1),$$
and hence
$$\boxed{
\Phi\!\left(B+\bigcup_iP_i\right)-\Phi(B)=n.}$$
8. Reclassifying the other pairs as old gives exactly  $2-n$ Let
$$B'=B+\bigcup_{i=1}^{n-1}P_i.$$
The retained pairs have no foreign contacts with each other: all foreign contacts in the full construction require  $V_0$ . Their combined gain over  $B$  is therefore
$$\Phi(B')-\Phi(B)=2(n-1).$$
Subtracting this from the full simultaneous gain gives
$$\boxed{
\Phi(B'+P_0)-\Phi(B')
=n-2(n-1)=2-n.}$$
Equivalently,  $P_0$  has local gain  $1$  and acquires  $n-1$  old/new contact debits. Its adjustment relative to the enlarged baseline is
$$a_0=(2-n)-1=1-n.$$
The old roots’ earlier gains are already contained in—and subtracted with— $\Phi(B')$ . They cannot be spent again to declare this later marginal nonnegative. This is exactly the distinction the obstruction is meant to establish.No complete-extension assumption occurs in the construction or either gain calculation.9. Scope of the formal and reported checksThe displayed Lean statements support the advertised interval packing, anchor uniqueness, bar precedence, near-column coverage, eligible-root credit, and ledger arithmetic. Their scope is correctly limited. In particular, unbounded_one_consumer_family proves the arithmetic identity
$$(2n-1)-(n-1)=n;$$
the full source construction and its disjointness still require the written argument.The event partition, contact correction, and all- $n$  source argument above supply the needed general reasoning independently of the reported finite runs.The mathematical claim is accepted. Correct the “four rows after the preceding root far tip” sentence, and keep the packing lemma explicitly in the stipulated downward EAST phase. The accepted conclusion retains  $\sum_i a_i$ ; the same valid construction shows why arbitrary old-baseline monotonicity cannot replace it.
